issues.legal_issue: A person in established possession may obtain protection against interference by someone not shown to have a better title, even if the person's own title is not satisfactorily proved.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought a permanent injunction against interference with the site.
The trial court and first appellate court found, on the evidence, that the plaintiff had possessed the site since purchasing it.
The defendant's better title to the site had not been established.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was entitled to the injunction protecting his possession, notwithstanding the failure to satisfactorily prove title.
issues.legal_principle: Possession is an important circumstance and may be protected against interference by a person who is not proved to have a better title. No provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.

predicates.injunction_suit: The proceeding seeks an injunction to prevent interference with possession of property.
predicates.plaintiff_in_possession: The person seeking the injunction is found to have possessed the property.
predicates.defendant_better_title_unproved: The person accused of interference is not proved to have a better title to the property.

issues.definition: When an injunction suit concerns a plaintiff found in possession and the defendant is not proved to have a better title, the plaintiff's possession is protected by an injunction.

issues.legal_issue: A declaration of ownership cannot be granted when the claimant has not satisfactorily established title to the property.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought a declaration that he was the absolute owner of the site.
The High Court concluded, and the Supreme Court agreed, that the material on record did not satisfactorily establish the plaintiff's title.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was not entitled to the declaration of ownership, and the suit was dismissed to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: A claimant seeking a declaration of ownership must satisfy the court that the claimant has good title to the property. No provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.

predicates.ownership_declaration_sought: The claimant seeks a declaration that the claimant owns the property.
predicates.title_not_satisfactorily_proved: The evidence does not satisfactorily establish the claimant's title to the property.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks an ownership declaration but has not satisfactorily proved title, the declaration is denied.

issues.legal_issue: When a judgment expressly leaves the question of title open, a later suit for possession based on title is not barred on the grounds of res judicata or Order II Rule 8.
material_facts: The court expressly left the question of title open for the parties to pursue in fresh proceedings.
The court stated that the plaintiff and successors could not resist a future suit by the defendant and successors for possession based on title on the grounds of res judicata or Order II Rule 8.
issues.conclusion: A future suit for possession based on title could not be resisted on those grounds.
issues.legal_principle: Where the judgment expressly leaves title open for determination in fresh proceedings, the later possession suit based on title is not barred by res judicata or Order II Rule 8. No earlier case was cited.

predicates.later_possession_suit_based_on_title: A later proceeding seeks possession of property on the basis of title.
predicates.title_question_expressly_left_open: The earlier judgment expressly leaves the question of title open for determination in fresh proceedings.

issues.definition: If a later proceeding seeks possession based on title and the earlier judgment expressly left title open, the later proceeding is not barred on the grounds identified in that judgment.
